blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Construction Project Manager Cost in Melbourne in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Wondering what a construction project manager costs in Melbourne? We break down typical fees, what you get, and how Millar Projects keeps your Southbank build on budget.
body: If you're planning a new home, townhouse development, or commercial fit-out in Melbourne, one of the first questions is: how much does a construction project manager cost? In Southbank and surrounding suburbs like South Melbourne and Port Melbourne, fees typically range from 5% to 15% of the total build cost, depending on complexity. At Millar Projects, we offer transparent fixed-fee packages starting from $15,000 for full project management, so there are no nasty surprises down the track.

The cost of a project manager isn't just a line item — it's an investment that saves you money in the long run. A good PM prevents costly delays, catches design errors early, and keeps trades accountable. In Victoria, where building standards are strict and weather can affect scheduling, having an experienced consultant on-site daily is worth every cent. We've seen clients save 10–20% on their build simply by avoiding rework and negotiation headaches.

Your project manager's fee also depends on the scope. For a medium-rise apartment block in Southbank, you'll need more coordination — structural engineering, council approvals, and multiple subcontractors — driving the fee upward. For a single townhouse in Richmond, a streamlined service might cost less. Millar Projects tailors its pricing to your specific project, not a one-size-fits-all quote.

Another factor is the level of involvement. Some PMs just attend site meetings and send reports. We take a different approach: our consultants are on-site daily, sometimes even picking up tools to keep things moving. This hands-on style reduces miscommunication and accelerates problem-solving, which directly controls costs. In our experience, the best PM is the one who's not afraid to get dirty.

Don't forget additional services like feasibility studies, structural investigations, or council liaison. These can add $2,000–$10,000 depending on complexity. At Millar Projects, we bundle these into our full consultancy package for a predictable price. And we always start with a free initial consultation — no obligation, just a chat about your plans and how we can help.

The key takeaway: the cost of a construction project manager in Melbourne is an investment in certainty. With Millar Projects, you get clear upfront pricing, daily on-site presence, and a team that treats your project like their own. Get in touch for a free quote tailored to your Southbank or Melbourne development.

blogPosts.title: Top 5 Reasons Your Southbank Townhouse Needs a Structural Engineer
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking of building a townhouse in Southbank? A structural engineer isn't optional. Here's why — and how Millar Projects' engineers prevent costly mistakes.
body: Southbank is one of Melbourne's most dynamic suburbs for townhouse developments, with tight sites, mixed soil conditions, and strict council overlays. If you're planning a townhouse here, skimping on structural engineering is a recipe for disaster. At Millar Projects, we've seen projects go sideways because the foundations weren't designed for the actual ground conditions — especially on redeveloped industrial land near the Yarra River.

Reason one: soil instability. Many Southbank sites have been filled or previously built on, leading to variable bearing capacity. A proper geotechnical report and structural design ensure your footings and slab won't crack or settle unevenly. Without it, you risk costly underpinning later — sometimes tens of thousands in rectification. Our engineers always recommend boring tests before any design work begins.

Reason two: council compliance. The City of Melbourne has strict requirements for structural safety, especially for multi-dwelling townhouses. Your building surveyor will demand certified structural drawings. Millar Projects liaises directly with council and certifiers to ensure your design meets all Australian Standards (AS1170, AS3600, etc.) without unnecessary delays.

Reason three: optimising your floor plan. A structural engineer can help you achieve open-plan living without excessive columns or beams, which is crucial on narrow Southbank lots. We use value engineering to reduce steel and concrete costs while maintaining strength. That's how we keep your build affordable without compromising safety.

Reason four: avoiding boundary disputes. Townhouses often share party walls or are built right to the boundary. Structural designs must account for existing neighbouring structures and prevent damage during excavation. Our engineers work with surveyors to map out load paths and protect adjacent properties, keeping you out of legal trouble.

Reason five: long-term durability. Melbourne's climate — wet winters, dry summers, and occasional heatwaves — puts stress on building materials. Proper structural design ensures your townhouse handles thermal movement, moisture, and loading over decades. At Millar Projects, we don't just satisfy the minimum code; we build for the long haul. Contact us for a structural assessment of your Southbank project.

blogPosts.title: What Does a Construction Feasibility Study Include? (Melbourne Guide)
blogPosts.excerpt: Before you buy a site or start designing, a feasibility study can save you thousands. Here's what Millar Projects covers in our Southbank-based feasibility service.
body: A construction feasibility study is the single most important step before committing to a build. It answers the big questions: Is this site suitable? What are the constraints? Can I make money? At Millar Projects, based in Southbank, we've conducted dozens of feasibility studies for residential and commercial projects across Melbourne, helping clients avoid expensive mistakes.

Our feasibility study starts with a site visit and analysis of physical conditions — soil type, slope, easements, and access. In Southbank, we often find services running through sites, contaminated soil from past industrial use, or flooding risks near the Yarra. We flag these early so you can adjust your design or budget before signing contracts.

Next, we review planning overlays and council requirements. Melbourne's planning schemes vary wildly between suburbs. A site in South Melbourne might have heritage overlays, while Port Melbourne has flood zones. We liaise with council planners to confirm what's possible, saving you months of back-and-forth later.

Cost estimation is a core part of the study. We provide a realistic budget breakdown based on current market rates for labour, materials, and consultants in Victoria. Our team also factors in contingency (usually 10–15%) for unforeseen issues like weather delays or supply chain hiccups. No pie-in-the-sky numbers — just honest projections.

Finally, we deliver a clear report with options: build as planned, modify the design, or walk away. The goal is to give you confidence in your decision. Many developers tell us our feasibility report was the best money they spent — it either validated their project or saved them from a money pit. At Millar Projects, we don't sugarcoat. We tell you the truth.

Ready to test your idea? Contact Millar Projects for a free initial discussion about your site in Southbank or anywhere in Melbourne. Our feasibility studies start from $2,500 and pay for themselves many times over.

blogPosts.title: Modular Construction in Melbourne: Faster, Cleaner, Smarter
blogPosts.excerpt: Modular building is taking off in Melbourne. Learn how Millar Projects uses off-site construction to deliver townhouses and apartments faster — with less mess.
body: Modular construction — building sections off-site in a factory, then assembling on location — is revolutionising Melbourne's residential and commercial sectors. At Millar Projects, we've embraced modular methods for townhouses and apartment projects in Southbank and beyond, because they cut build time by up to 30% and reduce site waste dramatically.

How does it work? Your modules are built in a controlled factory environment using precision tools and dry conditions. This eliminates weather delays — a huge advantage in Melbourne where winter rain and summer heat waves can halt traditional builds for days. Our factory partners in Victoria produce modules to exact specs, with plumbing, electrical, and finishes already installed.

On your Southbank site, we prepare the foundations while modules are being manufactured. Once ready, a crane places them in hours. This parallel process slashes overall project duration. A typical 6-townhouse development that would take 18 months with traditional methods can be completed in 12–14 months with modular construction.

Quality is another win. Factory-controlled conditions mean tighter tolerances, fewer defects, and consistent finishes. Our team inspects every module before it leaves the factory, so issues are caught early. On-site, we manage the assembly and connections, ensuring compliance with Victorian building codes and council conditions.

Cost predictability improves too. Modular construction has fewer variables — no stolen materials, weather damage, or trade scheduling conflicts. Millar Projects provides fixed-price contracts for modular builds, giving you peace of mind. In our experience, clients save 5–10% on overall costs compared to traditional stick-built methods.

Despite myths, modular doesn't mean boxy or boring. Modules can be stacked, angled, and finished with varied cladding to create unique designs. We've delivered sleek modern townhouses in Richmond and heritage-sensitive additions in Fitzroy using modular components. Want to explore modular for your next project? Call Millar Projects for a free consultation.
